subject: general
question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

I asked Mary if she would lend me a pencil.

options.text: I said, “Mary, will you lend me a pencil?”
I said to Mary, “Can you lent me a pencil?”
I said, “Mary, will she lend me a pencil?”
I asked to Mary, “Would you lend me a pencil?”

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** I asked Mary if she would lend me a pencil.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"if" indicates a Yes/No question**
 
 
• The conjunction "if" is removed. To form a direct question, the sentence must start with an auxiliary verb.
 
 
 
• **"would" becomes "will"**
 
 
• Because the reporting verb is in the past tense ("asked"), the modal verb "will" in direct speech changes to "would" in indirect speech. To revert it, "would" shifts back to "will".
 
 
 
• **Pronoun changes:**
 
 
• The third-person pronoun "she" changes back to the second-person pronoun "you" because the speaker is addressing Mary directly.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• The indirect "I asked Mary" is converted to "I said," placing "Mary" inside the quotation marks as a vocative (direct address).
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *I said, “Mary, will you lend me a pencil?”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** I said to Mary, “Can you lent me a pencil?”

 
 
• Uses the grammatically incorrect verb form "lent" after a modal verb (it should be the base form "lend") and incorrectly changes the modal to "Can".
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** I said, “Mary, will she lend me a pencil?”
 
 
• Incorrectly retains the third-person pronoun "she". When directly addressing Mary, the pronoun "you" must be used.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** I asked to Mary, “Would you lend me a pencil?”
 
 
• The reporting structure "asked to" is grammatically incorrect (it should just be "asked"), and it fails to revert "would" back to "will".
